rows.notes: Conference overview paper with no own data; all figures on water use efficiency (50-90%), yield, fertilizer and energy savings are taken from the IAI/FICCI (2016) strategy paper, Meti (2012) and Kumar et al. (2008). Not a primary study.
Yield increase figures (42.4% crops and fruits, 52.7% vegetables) are reported from the IAI/FICCI (2016) report; the paper conducts no experiment, survey or model of its own.
Reduced weed growth and reduced pesticide use are mentioned only as benefits cited from Meti (2012) and Viswanathan & Bahinipati (2015); no own data. Not a primary study.

The irrigation efficiency (50-90%), energy saving (30.5%) and fertilizer saving (28.5%) figures are quoted from the IAI/FICCI (2016) report in Section 2 and the Conclusion; the paper reports no measurements of its own.
Narrative review of micro-irrigation status, schemes and challenges in India; statements about water saving from root-zone application are assertions drawn from cited reports, not own results.
No primary data; the paper only asserts, citing others, that micro-irrigation relieves water scarcity. Nothing in the paper tests food production under low water supply.

notes: The cited study is a short conference overview (Kalpa Publications 2017) that synthesizes figures from IAI/FICCI (2016), Meti (2012), Kumar et al. (2008) and government scheme documents. It contains no own experiment, survey, measurements or model runs, so Q1 is 'no' for every row.
